title: Capacity Nexus: daily cluster/pool rollup (2026-12-29)
summary: Daily rollup of GPU utilization by cluster and pool with latency percentiles, queued job counts and headroom estimate. Exported from the cluster monitoring dashboard (combined timeseries). Purpose: ops morning sync, quick handoff to SRE and capacity planners. Includes surge flag heuristics and suggested redistribution actions.

notes: Surge_flag heuristic: YES when utilization_pct >= 85% OR queued_jobs >= 30 OR p95_ms > baseline*2
Pool headroom is (100 - utilization_pct) adjusted for reserved vs shared weights; quick estimate for ops to decide spillover
Interactive pools are priority for latency-sensitive routing; dedicated-ssd pools are enterprise reserved and should not be autoscaled down without SLAs
This export intentionally mixes percentiles and raw counts to make handoffs fast; follow-up query ids in linked_artifacts
Anomalies: cluster-na-7 interactive shows repeated canary runs from infra-experiments channel — coordinate with SE team before reclaim
action_items: (A) Rafael: throttle non-prod canaries on cluster-na-7 interactive for next 2h and report impact (JIRA-INF-7624)
(B) Maya: validate reserved commit utilization for cluster-eu-3 dedicated-ssd and open reclamation proposal if under 70% for 72h
(C) Tomás: add automated alert rule for queued_jobs >= 40 AND p95_ms > 50ms for interactive pools across regions
(D) Ops: consider temporary redistribution of 8 GPUs from eu cluster-eu-3 best-effort to cluster-eu-1 interactive if surge persists tonight
calculation_notes: avg_token_latency_ms is a weighted average across active slots for the 1h window ending 2026-12-29T23:00Z
pXX metrics are aggregated from per-request token-step histograms; p99 can be noisy for low sample pools (see row comment for best-effort low-sample warnings)
pool_headroom_pct includes a 5% safety buffer for autoscaler lag and scheduling jitter
